title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 59 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 425–427 (Night 59, continuing directly from nights-58), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 59 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The merchant dresses Nuzhat al-Zamān in costly clothes and jewels and leads her through the streets to Sultan Sharkān, her brother, who does not recognise her. He buys her, frees her, has the judges write the contract, and grants the merchant a tax-free charter. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالْخَمْسُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu wa-al-khamsūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the ninth and fifty,
sentences.i: And when it was the fifty-ninth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ كَتَبَتِ الْكِتَابَ وَنَاوَلَتْهُ لِلتَّاجِرِ فَأَخَذَهُ وَقَرَأهُ وَعَلِمَ مَا فِيهِ فَقَالَ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ صَوَّرَكِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna Nuzhata al-Zamāni katabati al-kitāba wa-nāwalathu li-al-tājiri fa-akhadhahu wa-qaraʾahu wa-ʿalima mā fīhi fa-qāla subḥāna man ṣawwaraki
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate-one, that Nuzhat al-Zamān wrote the writing and handed it to the merchant, and he took it and read it and knew what was in it, and said: Glory to him who fashioned you!
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Nuzhat al-Zamān wrote out a letter and handed it to the merchant. He took it, read it, understood what it held, and said, "Glory to Him who fashioned you!"
sentences.n: السَّعِيدَأَنَّ is printed as one word, السَّعِيدَ أَنَّ "the fortunate, that"; it is kept as printed. الْكِتَاب here is a written document or letter; the text does not say in this stretch what it contained. The shadda on صَوَّرَ is the print's own. The final كِ is the feminine "you", since the merchant speaks to her.

sentences.t: وَزَادَ فِي إِكْرَامِهَا وَصَارَ يُلَاطِفُهَا نَهَارَهُ كُلَّهُ فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ خَرَجَ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَأَتَى بِشَيْءٍ فَأَطْعَمَهَا إِيَّاهُ ثُمَّ أَدْخَلَهَا الْحَمَّامَ وَأَتَى لَهَا بِبَلَّانَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-zāda fī ikrāmihā wa-ṣāra yulāṭifuhā nahārahu kullahu fa-lammā aqbala al-laylu kharaja ilā al-sūqi wa-atā bi-shayʾin fa-aṭʿamahā iyyāhu thumma adkhalahā al-ḥammāma wa-atā lahā bi-ballānatin
sentences.l: and he increased in honouring her, and became treating-her-gently his day, all of it; and when the night came-on, he went-out to the market and came with a thing and fed her it, then made-her-enter the bath and came for her with a bath-attendant,
sentences.i: He showed her ever greater honour and spent the whole day in kindness to her. When night came on he went out to the market, brought back something to eat and fed her, then took her into the bath-house and fetched her a bath-woman.
sentences.n: أَتَى بِـ is "come with", that is "bring". أَطْعَمَهَا إِيَّاهُ, "fed her it": a verb with two objects, the second carried by إِيَّا. الْبَلَّانَة (the shadda is ours; the print has no mark) is the woman who runs the bath and washes the bather.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا إِذَا فَرَغْتِ مِنْ غَسْلِ رَأْسِهَا فَأَلْبِسِيهَا الْأَثْوَابَ ثُمَّ أَرْسِلِي أَعْلِمِينِي بِذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā idhā faraghti min ghasli raʾsihā fa-albisīhā al-athwāba thumma arsilī aʿlimīnī bi-dhālika
sentences.l: and said to her: When you-(f.) have finished from the washing of her head, then clothe-her with the garments, then send, inform me of that.
sentences.i: and said to her, "When you have finished washing her head, put the clothes on her, then send word and let me know."
sentences.n: He now speaks to the bath-woman (all the imperatives are feminine: -ī). أَرْسِلِي أَعْلِمِينِي, "send, inform me", sets two commands side by side with no "and"; read "send to inform me".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qālat samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And she said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: And she said, "With hearing and obedience."
sentences.n: A stock reply of assent. The accusatives stand for an understood verb: "I give hearing and obedience".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَحْضَرَ لَهَا طَعَامًا وَفَاكِهَةً وَشَمْعًا وَجَعَلَ ذٰلِكَ عَلَى مَصْطَبَةِ الْحَمَّامِ
sentences.tr: thumma aḥḍara lahā ṭaʿāman wa-fākihatan wa-shamʿan wa-jaʿala dhālika ʿalā maṣṭabati al-ḥammāmi
sentences.l: Then he had-present for her food and fruit and wax, and put that upon the bench of the bath.
sentences.i: Then he brought her food, fruit and candles, and set it all on the bench of the bath-house.
sentences.n: شَمْع is wax, hence candles. مَصْطَبَة is a built-in stone or plaster bench, here in the bath's outer chamber.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتِ الْبَلَّانَةُ مِنْ تَنْظِيفِهَا أَلْبَسَتْهَا ثِيَابَهَا فَخَرَجَتْ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ وَجَلَسَتْ عَلَى مَصْطَبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghati al-ballānatu min tanẓīfihā albasathā thiyābahā fa-kharajat mina al-ḥammāmi wa-jalasat ʿalā maṣṭabatihi
sentences.l: And when the bath-attendant finished from the cleaning of her, she clothed her with her clothes, and she went-out from the bath and sat upon its bench,
sentences.i: When the bath-woman had finished cleaning her she dressed her in her clothes, and she came out of the bath and sat on its bench,
sentences.n: The "she" of فَخَرَجَتْ وَجَلَسَتْ is Nuzhat al-Zamān; the subject changes without warning, as often in this text.

sentences.t: وَأَرْسَلَتِ الْبَلَّانَةُ أَعْلَمَتْهُ وَخَرَجَتْ فَوَجَدَتِ الْمَائِدَةَ حَاضِرَةً فَأَكَلَتْ هِيَ وَالْبَلَّانَةُ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ وَالْفَاكِهَةِ وَدَفَعَتَا الْبَاقِيَ لِصُنَّاعِ الْحَمَّامِ وَحَارِسِهِ ثُمَّ بَاتَتْ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-arsalati al-ballānatu aʿlamathu wa-kharajat fa-wajadati al-māʾidata ḥāḍiratan fa-akalat hiya wa-al-ballānatu mina al-ṭaʿāmi wa-al-fākihati wa-dafaʿatā al-bāqiya li-ṣunnāʿi al-ḥammāmi wa-ḥārisihi thumma bātat ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And the bath-attendant sent, she informed him, and went-out; and she found the table present; and she ate, she and the bath-attendant, from the food and the fruit, and the two gave the remainder to the workers of the bath and its keeper, then she spent-the-night until the morning.
sentences.i: The bath-woman sent word to tell him, and went out; and she found the table laid. Then she ate, she and the bath-woman, of the food and fruit, and the two of them gave what was left to the bath's workmen and its keeper. Then she slept there until morning.
sentences.n: I read the bath-woman as the one who sends word, as the merchant had asked, and "she found" as Nuzhat al-Zamān, since هِيَ "she" is added to her verb to set her beside the bath-woman; the Arabic does not make the change of subject plain. أَرْسَلَتْ أَعْلَمَتْهُ is again "sent, informed him" without a linking word. دَفَعَتَا is the dual feminine, "the two of them gave".

sentences.t: وَبَاتَ التَّاجِرُ مُنْعَزِلًا عَنْهَا فِي مَكَانٍ آخَرَ
sentences.tr: wa-bāta al-tājiru munʿazilan ʿanhā fī makānin ākhara
sentences.l: And the merchant spent-the-night secluded from her in another place.
sentences.i: The merchant spent the night apart from her, in another place.
sentences.n: The merchant keeps his word: he has bought her and does not touch her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَيْقَظَ مِنْ نَوْمِهِ أَيْقَظَ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ وَأَحْضَرَ لَهَا قَمِيصًا رَفِيعًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istayqaẓa min nawmihi ayqaẓa Nuzhata al-Zamāni wa-aḥḍara lahā qamīṣan rafīʿan
sentences.l: And when he woke from his sleep, he woke Nuzhat al-Zamān and had-present for her a shirt, fine,
sentences.i: When he woke from his sleep he woke Nuzhat al-Zamān and brought her a fine shift,

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَ كُوفِيَّةً بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ وَبَدْلَةَ لِبَاسِ تُرْكِيَّةً مُزَرْكَشَةً وَخُفًّا مُزَرْكَشًا بِالذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ مُرَصَّعًا بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadha kūfiyyatan bi-alfi dīnārin wa-badlata libāsi turkiyyatan muzarkashatan wa-khuffan muzarkashan bi-al-dhahabi al-aḥmari muraṣṣaʿan bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari
sentences.l: and took a head-cloth at a thousand dinars, and a suit of clothing, Turkish, gold-embroidered, and a boot, gold-embroidered with the red gold, studded with the pearls and the jewels,
sentences.i: and took a head-cloth worth a thousand dinars, a Turkish suit of clothes, richly embroidered, and a slipper embroidered with red gold and studded with pearls and jewels,
sentences.n: كُوفِيَّة is a kerchief or head-cloth. مُزَرْكَش (Persian zar, gold, with kash, drawn) is embroidered with gold thread. بَدْلَةَ لِبَاسٍ تُرْكِيَّةً: the feminine adjective belongs to بَدْلَة "suit", not to لِبَاس. بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ: the بِـ gives the price. The shadda on مُرَصَّعًا is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلَ فِي أُذْنَيْهَا حَلَقًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ مُرَصَّعًا بِلُؤْلُؤٍ بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿala fī udhnayhā ḥalaqan min dhahabin muraṣṣaʿan bi-luʾluʾin bi-alfi dīnārin
sentences.l: and put in her two ears rings of gold, studded with pearls, at a thousand dinars,
sentences.i: and put in her ears gold rings set with pearls, worth a thousand dinars,

sentences.t: وَوَضَعَ فِي رَقَبَتِهَا طَوْقًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ بَيْنَ الرُّمَّانَتَيْنِ وَقِلَادَةً مِنْ عَنْبَرٍ تَضْرِبُ تَحْتَ نَهْدَيْهَا فَوْقَ سُرَّتِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-waḍaʿa fī raqabatihā ṭawqan min dhahabin bayna al-rummānatayni wa-qilādatan min ʿanbarin taḍribu taḥta nahdayhā fawqa surratihā
sentences.l: and put on her neck a collar of gold between the two pomegranates, and a necklace of ambergris that strikes beneath her two breasts above her navel.
sentences.i: and put round her neck a gold collar between the two pomegranates, and a necklace of ambergris that fell beneath her breasts, above her navel.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ الرُّمَّانَتَيْنِ, "between the two pomegranates", is obscure: perhaps two pomegranate-shaped ornaments on the collar, or the collar set between them. Take it as uncertain. تَضْرِبُ "strikes" is used of something that hangs down and swings against the body; عَنْبَر is ambergris, whose scent was prized in necklaces.

sentences.t: وَتِلْكَ الْقِلَادَةُ فِيهَا عَشْرُ أُكَرٍ وَتِسْعَةُ أَهِلَّةٍ كُلُّ هِلَالٍ فِي وَسْطِهِ فَصٌّ مِنْ يَا قُوتٍ وَكُلُّ أُكْرَةٍ فِيهَا فَصٌّ مِنَ الْبَلَخْشِ
sentences.tr: wa-tilka al-qilādatu fīhā ʿashru ukarin wa-tisʿatu ahillatin kullu hilālin fī wasaṭihi faṣṣun min yā qūtin wa-kullu ukratin fīhā faṣṣun mina al-balakhshi
sentences.l: And that necklace, in it are ten balls and nine crescents; each crescent, in its middle is a gem of ruby, and each ball, in it is a gem of the balas-ruby.
sentences.i: That necklace held ten balls and nine crescents. In the middle of each crescent was a ruby, and in each ball a balas ruby.
sentences.n: يَا قُوت ("ruby", from Greek) is printed as two words; it is one. الْبَلَخْش (balas ruby, a pale red spinel, named from Badakhshān) is the second stone. The ten balls and nine crescents are the beads and pendants strung on the necklace.

sentences.t: وَثَمَنُ تِلْكَ الْقِلَادَةِ ثَلٰثَةُ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ وَكُلُّ أُكْرَةٍ بِعِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-thamanu tilka al-qilādati thalāthatu ālāfi dīnārin wa-kullu ukratin bi-ʿishrīna alfa dirhamin
sentences.l: And the price of that necklace was three thousands of dinars, and each ball at twenty thousand dirhams.
sentences.i: The price of that necklace was three thousand dinars, and each ball was worth twenty thousand dirhams.
sentences.n: ثَلٰثَة is printed ثلثة, a defective spelling, so it takes the dagger alif. بِعِشْرِينَ: the بِـ gives the price, "at", and the sentence has no verb "is".

sentences.t: فَصَارَتِ الْكِسْوَةُ الَّتِي كَسَاهَا إِيَّاهَا بِجُمْلَةٍ بَلِيغَةٍ مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣārati al-kiswatu allatī kasāhā iyyāhā bi-jumlatin balīghatin mina al-māli
sentences.l: So the clothing which he clothed her with, it, became at a sum, ample, of the money.
sentences.i: So the outfit he had put on her came to a very large sum of money.
sentences.n: صَارَ بِـ is "come to, amount to". كَسَاهَا إِيَّاهَا: "clothed her it", two objects again, the second carried by إِيَّا.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا لَبِسَهَا أَمَرَهَا التَّاجِرُأَنْ تَتَزَيَّنَ فَتَزَيَّنَتْ بِأَحْسَنِ الزِّينَةِ وَأَرْخَتْ عَلَى عَيْنَيْهَا خَاقُونِيَّةً وَمَشَتْ وَمَشَى التَّاجِرُ قُدَّامَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā labisahā amarahā al-tājiru an tatazayyana fa-tazayyanat bi-aḥsani al-zīnati wa-arkhat ʿalā ʿaynayhā khāqūniyyatan wa-mashat wa-mashā al-tājiru quddāmahā
sentences.l: And when she put-it-on, the merchant commanded her that she adorn herself, and she adorned herself with the best of the adornment, and let-down over her two eyes a khāqūniyya, and walked, and the merchant walked in front of her.
sentences.i: When she had put it on, the merchant told her to adorn herself, and she adorned herself in the finest finery, let a veil fall over her eyes, and walked, with the merchant walking before her.
sentences.n: التَّاجِرُأَنْ is printed as one word, التَّاجِرُ أَنْ "the merchant, that"; it is kept as printed. لَبِسَهَا is printed without the tāʾ that a feminine subject would take (لَبِسَتْهَا); it is read as printed and understood as "she put it on". خَاقُونِيَّة, a face-veil of the kind called after the Khāqān (a Turkic ruler), is my best reading; the word is uncertain.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَايَنَهَا النَّاسُ بَهِتُوا فِي حُسْنِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿāyanahā al-nāsu bahitū fī ḥusnihā
sentences.l: And when the people beheld her, they were-dumbfounded in her beauty.
sentences.i: When the people saw her they were struck dumb at her beauty.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ يَا بَخْتَ مَنْ كَانَتْ هٰذِهِ عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū tabāraka Allāhu aḥsanu al-khāliqīna yā bakhta man kānat hādhihi ʿindahu
sentences.l: And they said: Blessed-be God, best of the creators! O luck of whom this-one was with-him!
sentences.i: And they said, "Blessed be God, the best of creators! How fortunate the man who has her!"
sentences.n: The onlookers speak. تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ "Blessed be God, the best of creators" echoes the Qur'an (23:14) and is the stock exclamation at a marvel. يَا بَخْتَ مَنْ is the exclamatory "O the luck of him who ..." with the noun in the accusative.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ التَّاجِرُ يَمْشِي وَهِيَ تَمْشِي خَلْفَهُ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلَ عَلَى السُّلْطَانِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla al-tājiru yamshī wa-hiya tamshī khalfahu ilā an dakhala ʿalā al-sulṭāni Sharkāna
sentences.l: And the merchant did-not cease walking, and she walking behind him, until he entered upon the sultan Sharkān,
sentences.i: The merchant walked on, with her following behind him, until he came into the presence of the sultan Sharkān,
sentences.n: مَا زَالَ plus an imperfect means "kept on doing". The name is شَرْكَانَ (Sharkān), a diptote, hence the -a ending.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَالَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ، السَّعِيدُ أَتَيْتُ إِلَيْكَ بِهَدِيَّةٍ غَرِيبَةِ الْأَوْصَافِ مَعْدُودَةِ الْمِثَالِ فِي هٰذَا الزَّمَانِ حَازَتِ الْحُسْنَ وَالْإِحْسَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala ʿalā al-maliki qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-qāla ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu atytu ilayka bi-hadiyyatin gharībati al-awṣāfi maʿdūdati al-mithāli fī hādhā al-zamāni ḥāzati al-ḥusna wa-al-iḥsāna
sentences.l: And when he entered upon the king, he kissed the ground between his two hands and said: O king, the fortunate-one, I have come to you with a gift, strange of qualities, counted unique-of-example in this age, that has won beauty and benefaction.
sentences.i: When he came before the king he kissed the ground in front of him and said, "O fortunate king, I have brought you a gift of wondrous qualities, counted without a match in this age, one that has won both beauty and grace."
sentences.n: The comma after الْمَلِكُ is the print's own; the address runs on into السَّعِيدُ. غَرِيبَةِ الْأَوْصَافِ and مَعْدُودَةِ الْمِثَالِ are "adjective + genitive" chains describing the gift. The last clause حَازَتِ ... is a further description of the gift ("possessing, having won"). Read the sentence-end rhyme: -āni / -āna.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ أَرِنِي إِيَّاهَا عِيَانًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku arinī iyyāhā ʿiyānan
sentences.l: And the king said to him: Show-me her, in-plain-sight.
sentences.i: The king said to him, "Show her to me, so that I see her with my own eyes."
sentences.n: إِيَّاهَا is the separate pronoun "her", used because أَرَى ("show") takes two objects: me, and her. عِيَانًا is "by eyesight, openly".

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ التَّاجِرُ وَأَتَى بِهَا وَهِيَ خَلْفَهُ إِلَى أَنْ أَوْقَفَهَا قُدَّامَ الْمَلِكِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja al-tājiru wa-atā bihā wa-hiya khalfahu ilā an awqafahā quddāma al-maliki Sharkāna
sentences.l: And the merchant went-out and came with her, she behind him, until he made-her-stand in-front-of the king Sharkān.
sentences.i: The merchant went out and brought her in, with her following behind him, and stood her before King Sharkān.
sentences.n: أَتَى بِـ is "come with" and so "bring"; the verb chooses the preposition.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا حَنَّ الدَّمُ إِلَى الدَّمِ وَكَانَتْ قَدْ فَارَقَتْهُ وَهِيَ صَغِيرَةٌ وَلَمْ يَنْظُرْهَا لِأَنَّهُ بَعْدَ مُضِيِّ مُدَّةٍ مِنْ وِلَادَتِهَا سَمِعَ أَنَّ لَهُ أُخْتًا تُسَمَّى نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ وَأَخًا يُسَمَّى ضُؤَ الْمَكَانِ فَكَانَ يُبْغِضُهُمَا لِأَجْلِ الْمَمْلَكَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā ḥanna al-damu ilā al-dami wa-kānat qad fāraqathu wa-hiya ṣaghīratun wa-lam yanẓurhā li-annahu baʿda muḍiyyi muddatin min wilādatihā samiʿa anna lahu ukhtan tusammā Nuzhata al-Zamāni wa-akhan yusammā Ḍawʾa al-Makāni fa-kāna yubghiḍuhumā li-ajli al-mamlakati
sentences.l: And when he saw her, the blood yearned to the blood — and she had parted from him, and she small, and he had not looked on her, because after the passing of a span from her birth he heard that to-him was a sister called Nuzhat al-Zamān and a brother called Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and he used-to-hate them two for the sake of the kingdom —
sentences.i: As soon as he saw her, blood stirred toward blood. She had been taken from him while she was small, and he had never set eyes on her; for some time after her birth he had heard that he had a sister named Nuzhat al-Zamān and a brother named Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and he had hated them both on account of the kingdom.
sentences.n: حَنَّ الدَّمُ إِلَى الدَّمِ, "blood yearned toward blood", is the idiom for the pull of kinship, here felt before he knows who she is. The brother's name is printed ضؤ, with the waw of ضَوْء dropped; the vocalisation follows the print and the name is read Ḍawʾ al-Makān. لِأَنَّهُ ... سَمِعَ is a long "because" clause: because he had heard of them and hated them, he never sought them out (the reason given in the next sentence).

sentences.t: فَهٰذَا سَبَبُ قِلَّةِ مَعْرِفَتِهِ بِهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā sababu qillati maʿrifatihi bihimā
sentences.l: And this was the cause of the fewness of his knowing of them two.
sentences.i: That was why he knew so little of them.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ لَمَّا قَدَّمَهَا إِلَيْهِ التَّاجِرُ قَالَ لَهُ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ إِنَّهَا مَعَ كَوْنِهَا بَدِيعَةَ الْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ بِحَيْثُ لَا نَظِيرَ لَهَا فِي عَصْرِهَا تَعْرِفُ جَمِيعَ الْعُلُومِ الدِّينِيَّةِ وَالدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ وَالسِّيَاسِيَّةِ وَالرِّيَاضِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika lammā qaddamahā ilayhi al-tājiru qāla lahu yā malika al-zamāni innahā maʿa kawnihā badīʿata al-ḥusni wa-al-jamāli bi-ḥaythu lā naẓīra lahā fī ʿaṣrihā taʿrifu jamīʿa al-ʿulūmi al-dīniyyati wa-al-dunyawiyyati wa-al-siyāsiyyati wa-al-riyāḍiyyati
sentences.l: So at that, when the merchant presented her to him, he said to him: O king of the age, she — together-with her being wondrous of beauty and loveliness, such-that there is no peer for her in her time — knows all the sciences: the religious and the worldly and the political and the mathematical.
sentences.i: Then, when the merchant presented her to him, he said, "O King of the Age, besides being a wonder of beauty and loveliness, without her equal in her time, she knows every science, religious and worldly, political and mathematical."
sentences.n: The first قَالَ لَهُ has the merchant as subject and the king as the one addressed. يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ is simply the king's title as an address ("King of the Age"), not a name. بِحَيْثُ is "in such a way that". الرِّيَاضِيَّةِ are the disciplines of mathematics and the like.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ لِلتَّاجِرِ خُذْ ثَمَنَهَا مِثْلَ مَا اشْتَرَيْتَهَا وَدَعْهَا وَرُحْ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku li-al-tājiri khudh thamanahā mithla mā ishtaraytahā wa-daʿhā wa-ruḥ ilā ḥāli sabīlika
sentences.l: And the king said to the merchant: Take her price, the like of what you bought her for, and leave her, and go to the state of your way.
sentences.i: Then the king said to the merchant, "Take her price, just what you paid for her, leave her with me, and go on your way."
sentences.n: إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِكَ, "to the state of your road", is a fixed phrase for "be on your way". مِثْلَ مَا اشْتَرَيْتَهَا leaves out the "for": "the like of what you bought her (for)".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً وَلٰكِنِ اكْتُبْ لِي مَرْقُومًا عَلَى أَنِّي لَا أَدْفَعُ عُشْرًا أَبَدًا عَلَى تِجَارَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan wa-lākini uktub lī marqūman ʿalā annī lā adfaʿu ʿushran abadan ʿalā tijāratī
sentences.l: And he said to him: Hearing and obedience! but write for me a writ, on-the-footing that I never pay a tithe, ever, on my trade.
sentences.i: He said to him, "With hearing and obedience. But write me a decree that I shall never pay duty on my trade."
sentences.n: سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً is an accusative of the "I do so with ..." kind: a formula of assent. مَرْقُوم ("something written") is a written order, a decree. عُشْر ("a tenth") is customs duty; the damma printed on the ع is the edition's own. عَلَى أَنَّ is "on the condition / to the effect that".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ إِنِّي أَوَّلَ مَا أَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ وَلٰكِنْ أَخْبِرْنِي كَمْ وَزَنْتَ ثَمَنَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku innī awwala mā afʿalu dhālika wa-lākin akhbirnī kam wazanta thamanahā
sentences.l: And the king said: Truly I — first of what I do — that; but inform me, how much did you weigh-out as her price?
sentences.i: The king said, "I shall do that first of all. But tell me, how much did you pay for her?"
sentences.n: أَوَّلَ مَا أَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ is awkward: "the first thing I do is that", with أَوَّلَ in the accusative as an adverb. The sense is "that will be my first act". وَزَنَ "weigh out" is the verb for paying in coin by weight.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَزَنْتُ ثَمَنَهَا مِائَةَ أَلْفِ دِينَارٍ وَكَسَوْتُهَا بِمِائَةِ أَلْفِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wazantu thamanahā miʾata alfi dīnārin wa-kasawtuhā bi-miʾati alfi dīnārin
sentences.l: And he said: I weighed-out her price, a hundred thousand dinars, and I clothed her at a hundred thousand dinars.
sentences.i: He said, "I paid a hundred thousand dinars for her, and another hundred thousand dinars on her clothing."

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ هٰذَا الْكَلَامَ قَالَ أَنَا أُعْطِيكَ فِي ثَمَنِهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِخَازِنِ دَارَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku hādhā al-kalāma qāla anā uʿṭīka fī thamanihā akthara min dhālika thumma daʿā bi-khāzini dārihi
sentences.l: And when the king heard this speech he said: I will give you for her price more than that. Then he called for the keeper of his house —
sentences.i: When the king heard this he said, "I will give you more than that for her." Then he called for his treasurer.
sentences.n: The print has دارة, with tā' marbūṭa, for دَارِهِ "his house"; it is kept as printed and read dārihi. خَازِنُ الدَّارِ is the keeper of the household stores or treasury. دَعَا بِـ is "call for", the verb choosing the preposition. The printed shadda on فلمّا is kept.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ أَعْطِ لِهٰذَا التَّاجِرِ ثَلٰثَمِائَةِ أَلْفِ دِينَارٍ وَعِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ فَيَكُونُ لَهُ مِئَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ فَائِدَةً
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu aʿṭi li-hādhā al-tājiri thalāthamiʾati alfi dīnārin wa-ʿishrīna alfa dīnārin fa-yakūnu lahu miʾatun wa-ʿishrūna alfa dīnārin fāʾidatan
sentences.l: And he said to him: Give to this merchant three-hundred of thousand of dinar and twenty thousand of dinar, so there will be to him a hundred and twenty thousand of dinar, profit.
sentences.i: And he said to him, "Pay this merchant three hundred thousand dinars and twenty thousand more, so that he has a profit of a hundred and twenty thousand dinars."
sentences.n: The sums are given as printed; the text does not show the reckoning. In مِئَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ the one "thousand" counts for the whole number, "a hundred and twenty thousand". فَيَكُونُ is read as an indicative, "and so there is to him"; Classical grammar would put a subjunctive after a command. فَائِدَةً, "profit", is accusative as the thing he ends up with.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَحْضَرَ السُّلْطَانُ شَرْكَانُ الْقُضَاةَ الْأَرْبَعَةَ وَسَلَّمَهُ الْمَالَ بِحَضْرَتِهِمْ وَقَالَ لِلْقُضَاةِ أُشْهِدُكُمْ إِنِّي أَعْتَقْتُ جَارِيَتِي هٰذِهِ وَأُرِيدُأَنْ أَتَزَوَّجَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma aḥḍara al-sulṭānu Sharkānu al-quḍāta al-arbaʿata wa-sallamahu al-māla bi-ḥaḍratihim wa-qāla li-al-quḍāti ushhidukum innī aʿtaqtu jāriyatī hādhihi wa-urīdu an atazawwajahā
sentences.l: Then he had-come the sultan Sharkān — the judges, the four — and handed-over to-him the money in their presence, and said to-the-judges: I-call-you-to-witness that I have-freed my slave-girl, this one, and-I-want that I marry-her.
sentences.i: Then Sultan Sharkān summoned the four judges and handed over the money in their presence. He said to the judges, "I call you to witness that I have freed this slave-girl of mine, and I wish to marry her."
sentences.n: أَحْضَرَ (verb IV, "make present") is "to summon, have brought". وَأُرِيدُأَنْ is printed as one word, واريدان, for وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ "and I want that"; we keep the print and read it as two words. أُشْهِدُكُمْ (IV) is "I make you witnesses", the formula for calling witnesses to a legal act. Freeing her first is what lets him marry her as a free woman.

sentences.t: فَكَتَبَ الْقُضَاةُ حُجَّةً بِإِعْتَاقِهَا ثُمَّ كَتَبُوا كِتَابَهُ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-kataba al-quḍātu ḥujjatan bi-iʿtāqihā thumma katabū kitābahu ʿalayhā
sentences.l: So the judges wrote a deed, with her freeing; then they wrote his writing upon her.
sentences.i: So the judges wrote out a deed of her manumission, and then drew up his marriage contract with her.
sentences.n: حُجَّة (deed, legal document) is printed with the shadda, which we keep. كَتَبَ كِتَابَهُ عَلَيْهَا is the idiom for drawing up a marriage contract: "he wrote his writing upon her".

sentences.t: وَنَثَرَ الْمَلِكُ عَلَى رُؤُسِ الْحَاضِرِينَ ذَهَبًا كَثِيرًا فَصَارَ الْغِلْمَانُ وَالْخَدَمُ يَلْتَقِطُونَ مَا نَثَرَهُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَلِكُ مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-nathara al-maliku ʿalā ruʾusi al-ḥāḍirīna dhahaban kathīran fa-ṣāra al-ghilmānu wa-al-khadamu yaltaqiṭūna mā natharahu ʿalayhimu al-maliku mina al-māli
sentences.l: And the king scattered upon the heads of the present-ones gold, much; and the pages and the servants became picking-up what the king had scattered upon them of the money.
sentences.i: Then the king showered a great quantity of gold over the heads of those present, and the pages and servants began gathering up what he had scattered over them of the money.
sentences.n: رُؤُسِ is printed رؤس, without the second waw of the Classical رُؤُوس; we keep the print and read ruʾus. Scattering coins over a gathering is the traditional gesture at a wedding. صَارَ with a present verb, "became picking up", means "set about picking up".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ أَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ بِكِتَابَةِ مَنْشُورٍ لِلتَّاجِرِ بَعْدَ أَنْ سَامَهُ الْمَالَ وَكَتَبَ التَّوْقِيعَ مُخَلَّدًا بِأَنَّهُ لَا يَدْفَعُ عَلَى تِجَارَتِهِ عُشْرًا وَلَا مَكْسًا أَبَدًا وَلَا يَتَعَرَّضُ لَهُ أَحَدٌ بِسُوءٍ فِي سَائِرِ مَمْلَكَتِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika amara al-maliku Sharkānu bi-kitābati manshūrin li-al-tājiri baʿda an sāmahu al-māla wa-kataba al-tawqīʿa mukhalladan bi-annahu lā yadfaʿu ʿalā tijāratihi ʿushran wa-lā maksan abadan wa-lā yataʿarraḍu lahu aḥadun bi-sūʾin fī sāʾiri mamlakatihi
sentences.l: Then after that the king Sharkān commanded the writing of a decree for the merchant, after he had offered-him the money, and wrote the signature, made-everlasting, that he does not pay on his trade a tenth nor a toll, ever, and no one exposes-himself to him with evil in the rest of his kingdom.
sentences.i: Then, after that, King Sharkān ordered a decree to be written for the merchant, once the money had been tendered to him, and he set his signature to it in perpetuity: that the man was to pay neither tithe nor toll on his trade, ever, and that no one in the whole of his kingdom was to molest him in any way.
sentences.n: سَامَهُ الْمَالَ is obscure: سَامَ is "to offer, put a price or a demand to someone", so the sense is probably that the money was offered or handed to the merchant. Read with caution. مَنْشُور is an open letter of authority, a decree; التَّوْقِيع is the royal signature or endorsement that makes it valid. عُشْر ("a tenth") is the customs tithe and مَكْس the market toll. The بِـ in بِأَنَّهُ introduces what the decree says. The two negatives are in the indicative, as a standing rule.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ أَمَرَ لَهُ بِخِلْعَةٍ سَنِيَّةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika amara lahu bi-khilʿatin saniyyatin
sentences.l: And after that he commanded for him a robe-of-honour, lofty.
sentences.i: After that he ordered a splendid robe of honour for him.
sentences.n: أَمَرَ لَهُ بِـ is "to order [something] given to him", a different construction from أَمَرَهُ بِـ "to command him to". خِلْعَة is the robe of honour a ruler bestows on someone he favours.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: This is the stock close of a night: morning overtakes Shahrazād and she stops the "permitted speech", the story she was allowed to tell. شَهْرَزَادَ is the object and الصَّبَاحُ the subject placed after it.
